name: VPN Compromise Confirmed — Brute Force + Successful Login Same User
xql_query:
dataset = cisco_asa_raw
| filter _raw_log contains "109006"
| alter src_ip    = arrayindex(regextract(_raw_log, "from (\d+\.\d+\.\d+\.\d+)/"), 0),
        raw_user  = arrayindex(regextract(_raw_log, "for user '(.+?)' from "), 0)
| alter user_name = arrayindex(regextract(raw_user, "([A-Za-z0-9._@'-]+)$"), 0)
| filter src_ip != null
| filter user_name != null
| bin _time span = 30m
| comp count() as vpn_fails,
       values(src_ip) as source_ips
       by user_name, _time
| filter vpn_fails >= 3
| join type = inner (
    dataset = cisco_asa_raw
    | filter _raw_log contains "113039"
    | alter ok_user = arrayindex(regextract(_raw_log, "User <([^>]+)>"), 0)
    | filter ok_user != null
    | comp count() as vpn_logins by ok_user
  ) as ok user_name = ok.ok_user
| fields source_ips, user_name, vpn_fails, vpn_logins
description: Same user has VPN auth failures AND successful AnyConnect login.
alert_name: VPN Compromise Confirmed — Brute Force + Successful Login Same User
alert_description:
What fired: Same user has VPN auth failures AND successful AnyConnect login.

Why it matters: an actor is attempting to obtain or brute-force credentials. Assessed severity: Critical.

MITRE ATT&CK: T1110 - Brute Force (TA0006 - Credential Access); T1078 - Valid Accounts (TA0001 - Initial Access).

Investigate:
  - Identify the targeted account(s) and the source IP, and check for a SUCCESSFUL authentication following the failures.
  - Determine whether the source is expected; look for MFA prompts, password resets, or new sessions from the same source.
  - Pivot on the alert's key entity (xdm.source.user.username) to related activity in the same window.
  - Confirm the activity is not expected/authorized for the involved entity before escalating.
